Festive Vehicle Retail 2026 Hits Record 55.25 Lakh

India’s automobile retail market recorded its highest-ever 42-day festive sales in 2026, with 55,25,490 vehicles sold, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). This marked a 2.21% increase over the 54,05,956 units registered during the corresponding festive period in 2025. The industry added 1,19,534 units despite the high base of the previous festive season. Compared to Festive 2024, when retail stood at 44,57,691 units, volumes increased 23.95%, indicating a sustained expansion over two years.

🛡️ Your 3-Step Legal Rights & Defense Checklist

1
Light Meter Requirement:

Delhi High Court & Supreme Court guidelines mandate that traffic police must use an approved VLT Lux Meter. Any visual naked-eye assumption can be challenged.

2
Permissible Limits:

Front/Rear windscreens must have minimum 70% visual light transmission (VLT); side door glasses require minimum 50% VLT.

3
Virtual Court Appeal:

If challan is issued for company-fitted dark green tinted glass (complying with Rule 100), upload ARAI certificate copy on vcourts.gov.in.

✅ ACTIVE & ROAD LEGAL IN NCR
1,248 Days Left Before NCR Deregistration
Expiry Deadline: March 2029

📋 3-Step Protocol: Save Vehicle Value Before Ban

Step 1
Apply for Parivahan NOC Early:

Apply for RTO No Objection Certificate (NOC) at least 6 to 12 months before vehicle turns 10 (Diesel) or 15 (Petrol). Once expired, RTO will refuse to issue an NOC.

Step 2
Eligible Non-NCR States:

Cars can be legally re-registered in Rajasthan (except NCR districts), Punjab, Uttarakhand, MP, and Eastern UP without any age impound penalties.

Step 3
Scrappage Incentive Certificate:

If scraping with a Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facility (RVSF), obtain Certificate of Deposit (CoD) to get up to 25% road-tax concession on purchasing your next car.
